text_fidelity_a:
Bose QuietComfort 15 Acoustic Noise Cancelling Headphones (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I'm a software developer who works in a cubicle world with the heating system droning on above the ceiling (we're on the top floor of an office building - the HVAC is on the roof). These headphones provide an oasis of silence! The noise cancellation *seems* to be a cut above the others I've tried (Beats Studio at Target and a Sony set at Costco) although it's not really fair to compare as I didn't try the Bose under the same condition as the others (i.e. in a noisy store).

How good is it? The droning AC noise is completely gone. Voices I can still hear - until I play music. Even at low/moderate playback volume, voices are barely audible. People have to pat me on the back if they want my attention.

Comfort is excellent. I wear them on-and-off all day without problems. I imagine people with big ears might be less comfortable.

Power: the headphones use a single AAA battery. Keeping in mind that I maybe play music for 2-3 hours every day, the battery seems to last 2-3 weeks. As others have noted, these headphones will not work (i.e. play music) without power.

My one nitpick (and the reason I can't give it 5 stars) is the god-awful chord. It's some cheap plasticky material that I continually have to unravel by dangling the headphones by the plug end and letting the headphones rotate. It's really quite pathetic to put such cheap cr$p on $300 headphones - shame on Bose for not correcting this. Is it really going to affect your profitability so much you can't do something like the $20 Apple headphones that come with every iPhone (they're more rubberized and don't seem to get raveled).

Update for iPhone/iPad/iPod users: with iOS 7, Apple introduced a new way to invoke Siri (Apple's voice assistant) - instead of holding down the home button (or center button on the headphones) until you hear the Siri confirmation sound and then asking Siri your question and then waiting for Siri to accept your input, with iOS 7, you can keep the button pressed until you're finished talking - and avoid the delay Siri normally waits to know you're done with talking. It's a very useful feature.....and, it doesn't work with the Bose inline chord button :-( Not really Bose's fault, I guess, but I thought it worth mentioning.
text_fidelity_b: Bose QuietComfort 15 Acoustic Noise Cancelling Headphones (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Aurum Cables Pack of 2 AUX 3.5mm Male to 3.5mm Male Stereo Audio Cable - for iPhone, iPad or Smartphones - 12 Feet These are very handy to have to minimize (or eliminate) cord tangles. The coil is tight and holds its shape well. When "at rest" (e,g., not stretched) the cable is about 26 inches end to end. You can get it to 12 feet if you stretch it out fully, but the coil strength is such that it will pull whatever it is attached to. If you need the full 12 foot length, it would be better to get a non-coiled cable.

The ends are well attached, and the wire sheath seems pretty durable. Zero complaints about quality -- no crackling even when I jostle the ends while they are plugged in.

A great way to add some positioning flexibility for attached speakers without having to deal with excess cable that gets tangled. Highly recommend.

I’ve wanted to try a vertical mouse since reading about them, but for me, the DELUX Vertical Mouse won’t be the one. The mouse is just too big for my small hand. To give an idea of my hand size, I wear a size small women’s glove.

text_fidelity_a:
Panasonic HomeHawk Outdoor Wireless Smart Home Security Camera, Wide Angle View, Color Night Vision, 2-Way Talk, Works with Alexa & Google Assistant, 1 Camera Kit (KX-HN7001W) The Panasonic HomeHawk system has its good and its areas that could use some upgrades.
The good:
This is about as simple and install as you will get for a home monitoring system. No wires, five screws, charging the camera, downloading the app and you are ready to go, it is that simple. Once the cameras are charged and mounted I think it took me about 5 minutes to get everything running, and I am not technical by any stretch of the imagination.
The cameras are clear and provide good picture (you can select the quality of the picture when setting the system up) of the areas they are monitoring. Recordings are of good quality and clear, the night recording can be either color or black and white (infrared) depending on your choice.
Recording trigger areas can be set up along with sensitivity to movement in the recording area to trigger the recording to begin. All of these are very handy and easy to use.
The app is simple to use and pretty intuitive on how the system operates allowing almost everyone to use the system without any special knowledge. In all a good system for 95% of the people out there.
The things that can be improved.
It became apparent during setup of the outdoor camera (the one that looks like ET) that you need to mount it in a specific orientation, if you turn it over you cannot flip the image and everything will be upside down. If the ball neck for mounting the camera was just a little longer this would not be an issue as you could fit it under a soffit on your house wit a large field of view.
On the outdoor camera it works best when the rear of the camera is pointed in the direction of the base unit for connectivity. As you turn the camera and point the rear away from the base the signal drops pretty quick and the camera will not connect.
Other than these items the system is pretty easy to set up and use, now we see all the raccoons that show up to the house at night.
text_fidelity_b: Panasonic HomeHawk Outdoor Wireless Smart Home Security Camera, Wide Angle View, Color Night Vision, 2-Way Talk, Works with Alexa & Google Assistant, 1 Camera Kit (KX-HN7001W)

text_fidelity_a:
G.G.Martinsen Crystal-faceted 8 GB Mini Usb Port Multi-lingual Selection 1.8 LCD Mp3/Mp4, Video Player, Music Player, Media Player, Video player, Audio player With a Slot for a micro SD card--Black I have been offered three different G.G. Martinsen players free or at a discount in exchange for my honest review. I like this one better than the first one I got ([[ASIN:B0173CW2CQ an 8GB player]]), but because I went into detail in that review on the different functions (that this one also has), I've copied the functional descriptions from that review below. I'll just compare this one to the pink one in terms of what's different.

I like the black color of this, the ability to put it on a keychain or lanyard, and how small it is, but I don't like the way it all handles nearly as much as I do the [[ASIN:B0168C6MB4 16 GB player]] that I will review separately. The controls and settings are just awfully fiddly and not terribly intuitive. That you can add up to 16GB extra memory via an SDHC card (for a total of 24GB) is a boon, and that's the only thing I like better about this player than the 16GB one; the latter does not have an expansion slot. It's a useful thing if using a player like this when exercising if you can swap out different kinds of music for different types of activity—what works for running or walking will be different than what you'd use for swimming or dancing, for example. But still, these players all hold a decent amount of music natively, and you can also copy a ton of files to it if you're using it to double as a flash drive.

Here's the original functional review for this type of player:

The first thing I tried was the FM radio, because I was really doubtful it was going to work very well in my bedroom, but I was able to pull in NPR and the voices were crystal-clear. The earphones that come with this look really cheap, but they sound pretty good. As with any earphones, they don't cancel surrounding sounds, which makes them perfect for going out for a nice brisk walk. I actually prefer earphones to earbuds because earbuds never fit my ears right. These are like the original Apple earphones, and they stay in my smaller ears really well. I think it's a nice touch that these earphones are included with the player because you can use them in situations where you don't want your really good headphones to get lose or ruined. The device has the following menus, accessible by pressing the Menu button, then the right play button to cycle through them.

SETUP: It's very fiddly trying to set these settings. It takes a lot of trial and error to get it all to work. These are the settings: Clock, LCD Set (not sure what this is), Language (came set to English), Power Off (I can't figure out how to get into these settings to set the times to zero so the player doesn't shut off too soon, so this is why I'm knocking it back to three stars), an Online Mode, Firmware Upgrades, Memory Info.

MUSIC: Navigating through music is straightforward cycling through folders and files. I set up a Walking Songs folder and also dragged my whole Collective Soul Folder with Subfolders to the device, and I was able to navigate between the folders before playing. Selecting specific songs is more difficult. I've never learned how to create playlist files (I know, I know), so I can't say if those will work. There is a funky little equalizer animation on the screen when you play a song.

VIDEO: There's actually a nice music video included on the device, and it will play over and over if you don't stop it. I can see that this might make it possible to put together a loop of items to keep a child entertained on a trip, but it might also have utility for studying, memory work, a flash-card-like experience, or the like.

RECORDER: What it is. Records in .wav format at 32kbps. Great for quick reminders or embarrassing your friends.

VOICE: Used to play back recordings.

FM RADIO: Works great on the stations I've tried, without an antenna of any kind. I may have to start listening to more radio while I'm working.

PHOTO: A simple photo viewer, so you can keep all the pictures of your pets or kids that you'd normally have in your wallet to inflict on the people you meet. I'm just learning about QR codes (scanned my first one on my phone the other day), but I would think you could generate QR codes to carry on this device as well. The device does not recognize .png or .eps files, but it reads .jpgs fine, even larger ones (which do take a bit more time to load).

EBOOK: This is for reading simple .txt files. Don't think you can put anything proprietary like Kindle ebooks on it; it didn't read the .mobi file I copied onto it, or the .epub, or the .pdf. But who'd want to read a whole big book on such a tiny screen anyway? Use the EBOOK capability to take grocery lists or short paragraphs of instructions with you.

GAMES: I almost forgot the games. I'm not a game player. There are a handful of games that I haven't bothered to look at.

This player is not a super-fancy high-end piece of electronics, but it's a lot of bang for the buck and also something you wouldn't die over if you happened to lose it. Of course, you can always use it instead of a flash drive to take files with you different places for subsequent transfer. So it's a lot of functionality in one small package.
text_fidelity_b: G.G.Martinsen Crystal-faceted 8 GB Mini Usb Port Multi-lingual Selection 1.8 LCD Mp3/Mp4, Video Player, Music Player, Media Player, Video player, Audio player With a Slot for a micro SD card--Black

Anyway, unlike the other two players, the controls on this one make sense and handle more like what I'm used to. The instructions that come with this (that I also left at home!) were well-written in English, unlike so many products coming out of China these days. But I haven't needed the instructions to figure out how to use this player or change the settings. The first thing I did was set the Power Off and Sleep settings to 0 so the player won't shut off unless I flip the manual switch to turn it off. I have been listening to this player while I've been writing reviews, and I have had absolutely no cutouts with the FM radio even though I'm in a condo sandwiched on all sides by other units and this place is bad with reception of cable TV and other radios. I like that the station stays selected even when you power the player off and on again.

The control dial is easy to see, with a top Menu button, left and right arrows, and a pause/play button on the bottom (something the other players did not have). The round button in the middle has a good tactile feel, and even in the dark it's fairly easy to feel where to press for the different functions. I'll have to re-read the instructions to understand fully when to use the center button and how.

The little piece you can thread a lanyard into is plastic, but I don't think it will break easily unless you put a lot of stress on it. The player comes with a pair of original Apple-style earphones, which are great for walking outside where you need to be able to hear sounds around you while listening to music. The headphones are not the best in the world, but they are a nice additional feature and good to have in situations where you wouldn't want pricier headphones to get ruined (the gym, outside should it start raining). Of course, your listening experience will only be as good as the wired headphones you plug into this player. It really is a whole lot of bang for the buck and an attractive little player. I have the turquoise color, and it's really nice.

I put links to the other two players I have reviewed so you can compare them. What I like about this one is it doesn't have that gimmicky bubble-gum type selection screen but, rather, just has a list of the different features and functions. The list is easy to read and looks more businesslike and professional than the more cartoonish screens of the other two players.
text_fidelity_b: G.G.Martinsen Black 16 G Mini Usb Port Slim Small Multi-ling

text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Fire TV - 1st Generation I have some cognitive impairment and mobility challenges from lupus, and I was able to set up Fire TV really easily. The batteries go in the remote; the hdmi cable goes where it goes, and the power plugs in where it plugs in. The interface is simple and intuitive, and you can get everywhere with the home button, the directionals, back, and select. The only painful part for me/my hands was logging into my wireless network via the onscreen qwerty keyboard.

The screens are responsive with virtually no latency, thanks to the quad core processor and 2 gb ram. And video streaming is also very smooth. I have only been using this a day, but I haven't had it pause to buffer yet. I have a Chromecast in my son's room, a recent model Mac Mini in the living room, an older C2D Mac Mini in my room with Boxee on it, and a Raspberry Pi, and they all buffer at some point during just about every movie. I stayed in a vacation home with a Roku 2 last summer, and it was great, but it also had to buffer a lot. We also have three game consoles that have streaming video apps, and they buffer, too. I think the Fire's secret may be its wifi card. I am sure that, at some point, my ISP will find a way to slow it down.

So, yeah, I am giving the Fire TV four stars for doing exactly what I need it to do. I had come to Amazon to get another Chromecast, but I saw this and thought it would probably be better suited to what I need in my bedroom (I need my husband to be able to watch a tv show without my help - he is completely tech-challenged and cannot work the Dish remote - too many buttons).

The reason it doesn't get five stars is that there aren't yet enough content apps. There is a manga channel, a documentary channel, an art house channel, along with Crackle and Flixter and Plex (Plex is a for pay service that lets you stream your home content). There is plenty to watch if you are a Prime member (I am - and I appreciated having that already set up on my Fire TV - Thank you, Amazon!) I am also a Dish subscriber, with HBO and a Hopper. I have apps for those directly on some of my devices. I can get them on the internet on the tbs I have hooked up to computers. I can even blast them over to my Chromecast from my tablets. But they aren't on Fire TV, and none of my tablets will screencast to Fire TV. Soon as they are, this is a five star device for me.

I read in Entertainment Weekly that HBO and Amazon Prime have come to an understanding that will make lots and lots of HBO shows available through prime, which will also make them available through Fire TV. For the ones that are not, HBOGO will have an app for this. Between that news and my son's enjoyment of an eight dollar (as opposed to 40 to 60 dollars) platformed on this thing, I am adding a star.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Fire TV - 1st Generation

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Oasis – With 7” display and page turn buttons- Ad-Supported + 3 Months Free Kindle Unlimited (with auto-renewal) [[VIDEOID:a23b5cd930e819bd2cae7872ede2dd37]] I decided to finally upgrade my Kindle from the first Paperwhite when I found out I could get a 25% discount and a $5 Amazon gift card for trading in my very old and unused Kindle Keyboard 1st gen, as well as other bonuses of 6 months free Kindle Unlimited (approx $60) plus a 30 day Audible trial.

I’m very happy with it and it has some great features.
I do like the adjustable amber tint, but I also really like the ability to invert the colors to white print on a black background. This is even easier on the eyes, but it does have a noticeable (and irritating) white flash every few page turns when using the buttons, and almost with every page turn when advancing with the touch screen. I believe this is the e-ink refreshing. I will probably use the black inverted color only when I’m reading outside in bright sunlight.

I also am really happy to have buttons to turn the page again. It’s the ultimate laziness to be able to just keep your thumb in the button and depress it to turn the page instead of having to actually move your thumb a half inch to touch the screen, but hey, why move a half inch when your can push down 1/16th of an inch? All that extra movement add up over the years.
The real reason I like the buttons is this: I live in Alaska and we have very long, cold nights. But even in the winter, we turn down the heat at night. I read in bed every single night, tucked all cozy and warm under my down comforter... except for having to have my hand out in order to touch the screen on my Paperwhite to turn the page. My hand starts to get very cold. It’s uncomfortable. My half frozen hand takes away from my happy bedtime reading experience. With the Oasis, I can keep my hand under the blankets and just push the button. You don’t know what a big deal this is until you spend night after night with a frozen hand.

I also like that you can select which button to the the page advance button and which is the page back button. The Oasis comes set up with the top button as the page advance and the bottom as the page back, but I switched them: the bottom is the advance, the top is the back. I hold my ereaders at the bottom sides, and had to stretch my thumb to advance the page when it was set for the top button. It’s just easier and more comfortable to use the bottom button. And this is cool: the bottom button stays as my page advance button even when I rotate the Oasis 180 to use left handed!! Smart!!

Others have covered the size and weight so I won’t go it I all that except to say it’s comfortable to hold. I do use the official Amazon Premium leather cover and it fits perfectly, and the magnetic closure/sleep/wake functions work perfectly also.

Dislike: Nothing with the ereader itself, but with however Amazon picks the “special offers”. From what I read, these offers are supposed to be tailored off of a person’s reading history/preferences. I may be wrong.
The books they are featuring for me are “romance” genre. I am sooo not a romance genre girl. I don’t believe I’ve ever purchased this genre in my life. I’m a hardcore sci-fi/dystopian. I have an adverse reaction when I see romance special offer.

Other than that, some of the complaints by others leaves me wondering.
I just don’t think it’s THAT big of deal that it has a micro usb. Really, it’s just not that hard to figure out the big end of the cable from the small end. As for charging speed, charge mine while I’m sleeping at night so it doesn’t matter if it takes 1 hour or 4. I suppose having to carry a micro usb cord and charger when other devices use a usb-c cord/charger may be annoying but I think I can find 2 square inches in my purse/pocket/bag/backpack for it.

Also remember that this is an e-reader. It’s not a tablet, computer or smartphone, nor does it make any claims to be. Expecting an ereader to function basically like a computer/tablet/smartphone is expecting too much. It does an outstanding job at doing it’s job as an ereader.

I have sent many different type of files to my Paperwhite using my kindle email address and it’s worked excellent with that old ereader, so I expect this new Oasis will do excellent with those as well.

My suggestion is to read the description fully and know what you are getting and what you aren’t.
If your reading experience will be destroyed because this doesn’t have (nor claim to have) a usb-c, then this isn’t the ereader for you.
If you want it to be like a tablet or smartphone or computer, this isn’t the ereader for you.

But if you love reading and buy this for what it’s made for, I can recommend it.
Definitely look into getting a discount by trading in any unused kindles, and take advantage of the free Kindle Unlimited and Audible while they are available to offset the cost even more.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Oasis – With 7” display and page turn buttons- Ad-Supported + 3 Months Free Kindle Unlimited (with auto-renewal)

(Old Model) Seagate 1TB Desktop HDD Sata 6Gb/s 64MB Cache 3.5-Inch Internal Bare Drive (ST1000DM003) I had this drive and it lasted exactly 2 years from the manufacturing date on the case. No click, no warning, nothing. Just won't boot, won't format, won't do anything. I did manage to get the computer to recognize what the drive model is, using Seatools. So the CMOS is there, but the drive won't read or write any data. Seatools came up with the diagnostics that I have 3 bad LBAs. The drive has a warranty for 3 years in my case. But I got to thinking, that I get excited and send in my drive for a new one and next my identity goes missing. I cannot format or delete anything. If I destroy the drive, then the warranty is null. Seagate is not a good drive in my opinion.
Funny thing, I went and got a USB case that will accept any hard drive, ide....I put in an old hdd that I dropped on the carpet. It was absolutely dead--I thought. It was absolutely functional and all the data I thought I lost was there untouched. I am thinking about dropping this one on the carpet. But I found a place that I can use to get the parts and fix it myself--maybe with luck. If not, I will try the carpet idea.
text_fidelity_b: (Old Model) Seagate 1TB Desktop HDD Sata 6Gb/s 64MB Cache 3.5-Inch Internal Bare Drive (ST1000DM003)

text_fidelity_a:
Sennheiser RS 170 Digital Wireless Headphones (Discontinued By Manufacturer) I have owned these headphones since August, 2014. They are easy to use, and the sound quality is excellent. Prior to owning them, I tried out some $20 wireless headphones from a local drugstore which did not work at all, and I also did a jury-rigged setup with a very long, trip-hazard cable linking some headphones I owned to my TiVo. Never again. Both were a disaster.

This system is absolutely wonderful for two reasons:

First, I have weird hearing issues in that when I am trying to sleep, every little sound bugs me and I seem to hear even a conversation in the next room far more clearly than I have any desire to do, but when listening to TV, I can't understand 75% of what the actors are saying without captions. Go figure. With these headphones, no more problem. All dialog is clear as a bell.

Second, I no longer have to drive my husband crazy blaring the TV in order to adequately hear the actors speaking. By the same token, if my husband is watching a program on TV that I'm not at all interested in, I don't have to be subjected to listening to that either.

It's win-win.

I will say that I was not myself techie enough to install these headphones. My husband is an IT guy and he had to do it for me. So that's one downside for the customer who struggles with techie installations. Other than that, all is great.
text_fidelity_b: Sennheiser RS 170 Digital Wireless Headphones (Discontinued By Manufacturer)

SUPCASE Galaxy Tab S3 9.7" Case Unicorn Beetle Pro Series Full-Body Rugged with Built-in Screen Protector, Blue/Black (SUP-Galaxy-TabS3-9.7-UBPro-Blue/Black) When I ordered this, I didn't realize that I would be required to use the screen protector part of it. I thought that I could just slip on the back piece and use it like that. When I realized that both pieces are required (the back is too big and wouldn't stay on without the screen protector piece; hey, it's the first time I've ordered something with an integrated screen protector, so I didn't know), I wanted to send it back without even trying it.

I'm glad that I decided to try it for a couple of days, first. The screen is always covered with fingerprints and smudges and I find myself wiping it off many times a day. It also scratches easily. Since we're all washing our hands 40 times a day, the amount of fingerprints feels excessive to me and I hate looking at it. Even so, with the screen protector on, the screen is very responsive. Zero problems. And while I'm actually using my tablet, I don't notice the scratches or fingerprints.

There is also a shimmery rainbow effect. I don't really notice it while the screen is on and it seems to be less of an effect after the couple of weeks that I've been using it. I think because there's less of an air gap.

Everything lines up perfectly and the back part of the case also seems perfect to me. I would love to see this brand make a version that's just the well-fitted back piece.

So is it perfect? No. However, the things that bother me about it aren't really noticeable while the screen is on and I'm using it. It's protective and the screen protector doesn't interfere in the responsiveness of the screen in any way. So overall, I do think that this purchase was worth it. I'm glad that I decided to try it instead of immediately sending it back.

Another comment -- I keep a little piece of electrical tape over the front camera hole. The screen protector holds the tape in place so that I don't have to periodically change it anymore.
text_fidelity_b: SUPCASE Galaxy Tab S3 9.7" Case Unicorn Beetle Pro Series Full-Body Rugged with Built-in Screen Protector, Blue/Black (SUP-Galaxy-TabS3-9.7-UBPro-Blue/Black)

text_fidelity_a:
ASUS AC3100 WiFi Router (RT-AC3100) - Dual Band Wireless Internet Router, Trend Micro Lifetime AiProtection, AiMesh Compatible, Parental Control, MU-MIMO ASUS makes excellent routers overall with the added bonus of being compatible with a variety of free-ware router software like DD-WRT, Tomato, and Merlin-WRT (recommended). It includes all of the features you need for a proper home LAN, far better than the junky wireless routers offered by your internet provider, especially Comcast XFinity. (Don't believe the hype- their equipment is terrible.)

Some great features include
- Great 802.11ac support (5 GHz wireless support)
- Legacy 802.11b support (2.4 Ghz wireless support used in most cheap IOT devices)
- DHCP support which includes local DNS and MAC ID binding to make NAT and Firewall rules effective with having to manually configure your devices with easy to use client management
- Easy to use QOS with instrumentation features
- VPN support
- Many storage solution variants to allow for of personal cloud and LAN network storage (NAS-like functionality)
- Gaming networking enhancements galore
- Excellent security features
- Excellent compatibility with other devices
- Excellent and easy to use web-base administration software
- Excellent community support on countless on-line forums
- Best router for the money; Similarly featured Netgear routers are significantly more expensive without a real edge

Some downsides:
- Terrible vendor support (not really necessary unless you need a warranty replacement, but they are okay here)
- Some software limitations make many features will only work when you use local subnets within the 192.168.0.0/16 class B network
- Network storage throughput somewhat slow

It is devices like this that have had me a loyal ASUS customer for routers for nearly a decade. The fact that you can use Merlin-WRT as your software which IMHO more stable than the factory firmware makes it a slam-dunk.
text_fidelity_b: ASUS AC3100 WiFi Router (RT-AC3100) - Dual Band Wireless Internet Router, Trend Micro Lifetime AiProtection, AiMesh Compatible, Parental Control, MU-MIMO

Samsung 32GB up to 48MB/s EVO Class 10 Micro SDHC Card with Adapter (MB-MP32DA/AM) Deciding to catch up on my product reviews – I was ELATED this particular Micro sD card is no longer available. I know that’s a bit mean-spirited, but I can’t help it. I was out the money for the item because it was past Amazon’s 30-day return window.

I purchased one in October of 2015 for my Samsung GS4, and only two (2) months later – I needed a brand new one. Why? It failed. No warning, nothing. Just a failure.

And this wouldn’t be the first failure either.

The sD card I bought in December failed as well, but I’ll give it up for it – It went OVER three (3) years before failing. It failed April 3, 2019. I remember that because of the event it failed during. I would’ve expected the failure when I transferred the sD card from the S4 to the S8 in May 2018, but the card still worked.

There were no signs of pending failure or issues. The night before (4/2), it worked and I was able to retrieve some photos off of it.

My mother and I went to Knott’s Berry Farm for the Boysenberry Festival. And, any photos take before we left – GONE. No error messages – just gone. I didn’t know until I got home.

What photos I have were the return photos from the drive home. I had briefly
glanced at the card data (on my phone) at about 2pm, but after that (without being dropped, banged, over-heated) the card failed. I know some will ask why I didn’t back them up – I was in transit, driving on the freeway, so it wasn’t feasible.

All I know is that my photos were gone.

So, I had to purchase another sD card for my phone. This time I chose the GREEN Evo Select one. And, from April 2019 to the date of this review, it’s been pretty solid. Though I’m not taking any chances. I store photos to my S8 as well as the sD card.

Since it isn’t available, I won’t bother with saying I don’t recommend it. I certainly won’t buy it again if it does become available again.
text_fidelity_b: Samsung 32GB up to 48MB/s EVO Class 10 Micro SDHC Card with Adapter (MB-MP32DA/AM)

text_fidelity_a:
USB Power Strip Tower, BESFAN Surge Protector with 12 Outlets and 5 USB Ports, 10ft Extension Cord USB (Desktop Smart Charging Station) for Home, Dorm and Office As most of us know – if we have electronics (laptops, iPads, phones) – we need a surge protector.

And, since about 2003 – I’ve had TONS of them. Even ones that protected the landline cord (do we even have landlines anymore). I’ve had wide/flat, narrow/flat, and just ones that mounted to a wall.

I’ve had ones that didn’t have enough outlets either, or the outlets were spaced just “so” that I couldn’t plug up adapter type plugs (phones, etc). And, ones that the wall cord was so short they didn’t help out much in certain areas.

This one?

WOW! Game changer!

Not only the shape – I would never have thought of a tower design. But, it does save room. I have mine under my desk and with my old flat one – I ended up turning it off countless times. Not this one though. Outlets? 12 outlets which comes in handy, along with five (5) USB ports.

This is a LONG wall cord so plugging it into outlets further/farther away than where you need it is not a huge problem. Unless the outlet is across the room.

The outlets on this unit are spaced and sectioned for big or small plugs. And, the USB ports are a huge bonus! Some devices don’t come with a wall adapter and either you spend money on one, or you have to hook it up to your computer. This? That eliminates that situation.

I can’t attest to others’ and their phones – this charges my phone in the same amount of time as the wall adapter to the USB cord would. So, not much difference there.

Other than the cool stuff, this functions just like other surge protectors. No issues so far. It’s fairly sturdy and I’m definitely glad I got this! I’m definitely sold on this design and I plan to upgrade my household with them as I can.

I definitely wouldn’t hesitate to recommend this. Would make a great “house-warming” gift.
text_fidelity_b: USB Power Strip Tower, BESFAN Surge Protector with 12 Outlets and 5 USB Ports, 10ft Extension Cord USB (Desktop Smart Charging Station) for Home, Dorm and Office

text_fidelity_a:
Belkin 8-Outlet AV Power Strip Surge Protector with 6-Foot Power Cord and 2 USB Charging Ports, 3000 Joules, Black (BV108050-06-BLK) I love that this surge protector and plug strip has two USB ports for charging my Kindle and cell phone, but the placement of the USB ports, which is a major selling point for this unit, is hindered by the position of the cord wrap feature as well as the areas to plug in your larger electronics that have the big boxy plug. The USB ports are tucked right in between the cord wrap spot and the place to plug in larger plugs, so if one isn't blocking your USB ports, the other is.

In addition, I kind of wish that the majority of the plugs were spaced farther apart. I have a few electronics that have very small boxy plugs, and those don't fit right next to one another on the main area of the plug strip. The only thing that will fit on those plugs without overlapping are the traditional small plugs that are on lamps and other uncomplicated items. I don't have too many of those, and I'm guessing that most people buy plug strips because they have a bunch of electronics, almost all of which would have those bigger boxy plugs.

That said, the surge protector feature is absolutely effective, and I know this because we had PG&E replacing some poles in our neighborhood recently and we had many incidences of brownouts, surges, and spotty power, and this unit kept any harm from coming to any of my electronics that were plugged into it.

And while it is easy to make design suggestions, I have to say that I haven't found the perfect plug strip yet. Almost all of them seem to have some design characteristics that make them not quite ideal. While this unit is not perfectly designed with regards to the placement of the USB ports and the spacing of the regular plugs, it is certainly a high-quality, very functional unit that does what it says it does, and I trust the Belkin brand that it's going to function for some time. This plug strip is also nice in that it has a space so that you can mount it on the wall or on the back of your desk if you so desire.
text_fidelity_b: Belkin 8-Outlet AV Power Strip Surge Protector with 6-Foot Power Cord and 2 USB Charging Ports, 3000 Joules, Black (BV108050-06-BLK)

Kindle E-reader, 6" Glare-Free Touchscreen Display, Wi-Fi - Includes Special Offers (Previous Generation – 7th) I love reading, but I am consumed by a digital age. I spend so much time playing video games and on social media, I hardly give myself the time to sit down with a good book.

I have a phone, a computer, and a tablet, each with access to the kindle app, but the lights can often cause extreme fatigue when reading for long periods of time.
I could pick up physical copies of books and read those, but often times the font is too small for my bad eyesight, and larger books can be hard to read due to the pages curving.

Enter the Kindle. This ingenious little device fixes every problem I have experienced with digital and physical reading.
Because it does not light up, I do not experience the same fatigue as when reading on my other devices.
I have the ability to increase font size all the way to the point of each letter being about 1/2" tall. The flat design makes it easy to read in any position, I can even put it on a tablet stand and read hands-free!

It is extremely light-weight and does not cause my arms to become tired like large hardcover books do in some positions.

The library of books is incredible! I can read almost any book I want, though there are many that are not yet on the kindle store.

The battery life is phenomenal. I haven't charged it in 2 months and am just now getting a low battery alert! It takes a standard MicroUSB connection.

Over all, this is an excellent device and encourages reading in the digital age.

Canon EF 100mm f/2.8L IS USM Macro Lens with UV Protection Lens Filter The Canon 100mm f/2.8 USM macro is a lovely lens already, and Canon would need to significantly improve on it to make any owner of this lens consider selling in order to upgrade to the new L version. The new Canon 100mm f/2.8 L USM macro lens with image stabilization fits the bill and this particular 100mm macro owner, at least, decided to upgrade. I rented this lens at first to try out the new features, as my older 100mm lens is one of my most-coveted, most-used lenses, and I didn't want to give up on it simply because there was a new kid on the block. After the instant rebates came around I was in a well-enough informed position to make the purchase, and at a good price.

The aforementioned Image Stabilization is very effective in situations where you can't use the tripod, but want to maintain critical focus while working with shallow depth of field. The IS system in this lens, to boot, is an improvement on Canon's IS system found in other earlier lenses - Hybrid IS, a system which is particularly tuned to the demands of macro photography; I've tested this with the new lens and it's amazing what I can successfully capture handheld that previously absolutely necessitated a tripod. You can get the same results handheld now with approximately 3-4 less stops of light than you could previously. This perfectly suits my shooting style - I like to roam around, usually sans tripod, and take images in natural surroundings that may not always have the best available light. A relatively slow shutter speed to capture the scene in front of me usually meant I'd have to compensate by ratcheting up the ISO or go wider with the aperture, which are not always or often good compromises, for image quality reasons as well as for reasons of creative choice. The IS is a much welcome feature, and provides more leeway in variable lighting. Also sometimes people complain that the IS is too noisy when in operation; while that can certainly be true (I have a couple of other Canon lenses with IS), I have found that the new IS system in this latest lens is noticeably quieter - I'd call it pretty quiet, even with nothing else to compare it to.

Out of focus highlights - the bokeh - is smooth, smoother than the older version. Images appear very crisp, I'm pleased with the sharpness. The new lens is about an ounce or so heavier than the older one, not so much that you'd really notice. Also the lens, while a L, does not have the same build appearance as other L lenses - it is not hefty and metallic, and cream-colored. That doesn't bother me so much, but others more invested in the distinctive look of Canon L lenses might care. The lens body itself is sleek (compared to the rather portly older model) and has a nice matte black finish which you can handle easily - I don't quite know how to describe it - it doesn't have the usual "slippery" metal feel to it, so you don't feel like you might drop it if you aren't careful. Because it's an L, it comes with a lens hood; I always get hoods for my lenses, so I love it when a lens has one included!

One thing that is an interesting feature is that there are three settings for the Autofocus limiter (the older lens has two). It's basically there to help speed the AF in finding its optimal focus depending on which camera-to-subject distance you are shooting with - anywhere from strictly close up (.3 to .5 meter of distance) to full range. I'm still trying to figure out what real time difference it makes to choose between the .3m-to-infinity limiter and .5m-to-infinity limiter, but I assume it must make some difference for Canon to have included the additional option. Early days yet, I'll figure it out.

All in all - not every lens redesign results in a lens worth ditching an old model for, especially when the upgrade entails a bit more cost. But the new 100mm macro L is very much worth the upgrade, and the IS is a welcome addition to Canon's most popular macro option. Now if they'll just put IS in the 180mm...

I will also add that I made this particular purchase through the Marketplace seller J&R. I had no problems with them - delivery was swift and the item was well-packed.
text_fidelity_b: Canon EF 100mm f/2.8L IS USM Macro Lens with UV Protection Lens Filter

text_fidelity_a:
NETGEAR 8-Port Ultra60 PoE Multi-Gigabit Ethernet Plus Switch (MS108EUP) - Managed, with 4 x PoE++ and 4 x PoE+ @ 230W, Desktop or Wall Mount, and Limited Lifetime Protection I received this item through the Amazon Vine program, although the usual green writing may not be shown. The review is specifically for model: GS305EPP.

Port Binding: I noticed that the Netgear chart shows for the "plus" series of switches, that only models with 16 or more ports support port binding. However, through the web interface, I was able to do a single instance of port binding (it looks like it allows you to bind up to four ports, although I can't think of an instance where binding more than two ports on a five port switch would be worthwhile). I learned some quirks about port binding in the process, that using 802.3ad with multiple Linux servers doesn't allow for more than a Gb of data in any one direction anyway. BUT this switch does apparently support balance-rr, because I could get almost 2Gb/s over a 2Gb aggregate link. I think my hard drives in those machines were maxed out at that point. As I understand it, balance-rr has a high error rate because it uses striping and not all machines support it. But it was working quite nicely with my NAS units and this switch (I was expecting the 8 port switch, which would have made that setup more worthwhile because I could fatten the links on all three servers.

Although my current Netgear Pro AP does not have two ports for binding, I did have an AP before that supported it, in which case that feature on this switch may be an excellent option (particularly considering it is PoE). I haven't done the math for myself, but I think that port binding is almost a gimmick on APs because there is so much overhead on WiFi that even if your AP has a throughput in the multi-Gb range, enough of that is overhead created by the AP that you're not actually getting that much data from one computer to another.

Insight and Web Interface: The Insight App shows this switch (and my Netgear APs) as having "limited support" (just shows basic device info and a link to the device's webpage), so they're not really trying to get users of the "plus" line to subscribe to that in perpetuity.

And you don't need the app to use the switch. You don't even need the configuration page, really: I just plugged this into my old 24-port unmanaged Netgear workhose and it picked up an IP from the router and worked just like an unmanaged switch until I decided to give it a static IP and manage it.

I was really surprised how many features are packed into the management software, considering these are Netgear's lower line of managed devices. But most of the stuff you'll see on huge enterprise devices is here as well (well, it's been a while since I've been inside the big enterprise stuff, but all those goodies reach us as consumers before long).

The web interface is just like any other network device - you can reach it from any webpage and it is super GUI - probably just a little more than I really want it to be, but it is very intuitive and you can find everything with a few clicks. I say "super GUI" just because it looks fancier than I need it to. And one thing I find a little irritating is that when you expand one box, it collapses another, so you can't look at everything at once. This doesn't really matter, but I'm old school where I just want substance over style and even style that doesn't sacrifice substance still looks like they're trying too hard.

PoE: Clearly, on this 4+1 port switch, all four of your devices can use a full 30w each, so this is non-blocking in PoE+ as well as throughput. At time of writing, the 8 port with the same power budget was actually cheaper, so you might consider that, even if you can't use all the ports at full PoE.

What is great about this, is that besides just being able to add APs and IP cameras to your network (or even lighting, etc.), you can turn them on and off from the web interface. So I can keep my main AP on PoE (and therefore on my telecom closet's backup power supply), and then turn my detached garage's AP on and off from the web interface rather than having to go down to the basement and plug or unplug the PoE injector every time I want to use the garage AP (I just turn it on if I'm going to be working out there and might need to watch some "how-to" videos or control my audio system from the local LAN).

*Netgear, if you're listening, I would love to have a super lightweight (and free) app that works remotely (when not necessarily on LAN) to turn ports on and off for exactly this type of reason.*

Construction: Solid device, very dense and professional looking. Plenty of lights that tell you a lot from a glance. Power supply is external and about as big as the device itself. Would personally love a way to rack mount this AND the power supply (for maximum flexibility) in 1 RU, but of course I realize most people don't want to waste a whole rack unit on 5 ports. But for the space both pieces take up, it's about a mid size unit that could be mounted with "wings". It does have four-way keyhole mounts for wall-mounting.

Background: I have great experience with Netgear for my home (but way better than most homes') network. I'd definitely use all their devices were I doing work for small or medium sized businesses. I like them just a tad less when they start trying to sell you subscriptions (which is what I hate about Brocade and Cisco, along with all the proprietary garbage), but for the most part, Netgear is inexpensive and quite reliable. I've had a 24 port nonblocking unmanaged Gb switch running 24/7 in my dusty basement for over 15 years without a single fault AND they still sell that model. Their APs are the best I've had, and I don't think I've ever had a Netgear item break on me, period. I have had lots of other home/SMB stuff break or otherwise have strange issues, though.

That said, there's a lot of no-name PoE switches on the market right now. I don't need any of those handling my low voltage needs OR my data. And they won't beat this line on the price by too much anyway.

This is an excellent device which adds a lot of versatility to your network.

text_fidelity_a:
Bestlight 48 LED Macro Ring Light With 6 Adaptors Rings for Canon Digital EOS Rebel SL1 (100D),T5i(700D),T4i(650D),T3(1100D),T3i(600D),60D,60Da,50D,Nikon D5300,D5000,D3000,D3200,D5100 DSLR Cameras I've always wanted a Canon macro flash but the cost was just too much for something that I would not use very regularly. This macro light, while not a flash, is a very affordable alternative that works very well.

It is a 48 LED light. There's no communication with the camera - it's not a flash, nor can it be controlled in any way by the camera itself. The controls are manual, and allow you to use all the LEDs, half of them (left) or half of them (right). It is powered by 2 AA batteries or by an AC adapter (included). The battery pack mounts on the hotshoe, and the macro light is affixed to the lens barrel.

The battery pack fit fine on my Canon 5D Mark II, but the manufacturer includes a note with the device that says an additional adapter will be needed for it to fit the hotshoe of Sony, Konica and Minolta DSLR cameras.

It comes with two diffusers (white and orange) that are easy to put on and take off. It also comes with six lens thread adapter rings for all the usual sizes - 49mm, 52, 55, 58, 62, and 67. You attach the adapter ring to front of lens, and slot the light over the ring.

No problems fitting it to a Canon L 100mm macro lens. Fit well and was secure during use.

It throws a good amount of light on a ultra close-range subject, which may be otherwise shaded by the close proximity of your lens, or for other reasons be hard to light properly. But, there are limitations - don't expect this to throw a lot of light like a light panel would on a subject at medium distance.

The build quality is better than expected given the price. It's all plastic, but seems more than durable enough for home use.

I'm very pleased with this. It's a small fraction of the cost of a Canon ring light and, while it does not have flash capabilities, it remains a very helpful addition to lighting those tricky macro shots. Highly recommend.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: Bestlight 48 LED Macro Ring Light With 6 Adaptors Rings for Canon Digital EOS Rebel SL1 (100D),T5i(700D),T4i(650D),T3(1100D),T3i(600D),60D,60Da,50D,Nikon D5300,D5000,D3000,D3200,D5100 DSLR Cameras

text_fidelity_a:
Antennas Direct ClearStream 1MAX HDTV Antenna UHF VHF, Multi-Directional, 40+ Mile Range, UHD 4K, NEXTGEN TV – w/Adjustable Mounting Hardware (Black) Trying to decide if we were ready to cut the cord, we installed this antenna to see if we could get all the local channels. We got 40 digital channels about 20 miles west of Washington DC and the major networks are crystal clear.

The network towers we use are clustered together about 20 miles away. We have 2 or more topographical obstructions between our house and the towers (no line of sight). The Noise Margin on the networks is 35-40 dB. TVFool.com listed my location as "yellow" (which means use an attic antenna or higher). The cable drop is about 25 feet and I did not use an amplifier.

This antenna is supposed to be omni-directional but we did experience occasional signal drop on the networks with the initial "eyeball" installation (which was off about 15 degrees). Standing directly under the antenna and looking through a compass I had my son walk through the yard until he stepped into the path to the towers. Then I had him stand still, facing the antenna, and rotated it until he told me it was pointed straight over his head. That seemed to fix the signal drops. Given all the factors of our situation, I am probably maxing out the performance of this antenna. If I have any issues I'll just buy the add-on the reflector shield to increase directional performance...but for right now I don't need it.

Installation was easy (I just mounted it to the Direct TV mast). This antenna is small and light which was a big plus when climbing up a 25 foot ladder.

So far so good!
text_fidelity_b: Antennas Direct ClearStream 1MAX HDTV Antenna UHF VHF, Multi-Directional, 40+ Mile Range, UHD 4K, NEXTGEN TV – w/Adjustable Mounting Hardware (Black)

Canon EF-S 55-250mm f/4.0-5.6 IS II Telephoto Zoom Lens I'm very pleased with this lens given the price. Although it won't give a Canon L lens a run for its money, it's reasonable fast and has a nice range. The build quality is very good for this price point. Both the zoom movement and focusing are smooth. The zoom marking are well-marked. While the mount is plastic rather than metal, this keeps the lens weight down, which is always something that I appreciate. Despite being plastic the mount and housing are more than sturdy enough for even the most avid amateur photographer.

The image stabilization works very well and is an essential feature to have unless you have rock-steady hands.

I find the image quality to be excellent at all zoom ranges except for when it's at its max range, but even then it's more than acceptable.

It's certainly not the best lens that Canon makes, but I don't think there's another zoom out there that can match this performance at this price. It's a great second lens if you have a crop sensor body (such as the Rebel series) and the 18-55mm zoom (which is a common kit lens). The pair provides a wide range of shooting opportunities at a very reasonable cost. Highly recommend.
text_fidelity_b: Canon EF-S 55-250mm f/4.0-5.6 IS II Telephoto Zoom Lens

I plugged it back into my laptop where I knew it did work at one time, and sure enough, it doesn't work anymore.

So, basically it didn't function the way it should have, and within 6 months it just stopped working all together. Biggest waste of money, and now I can't return it.

text_fidelity_a:
Altec Lansing iM227 Orbit MP3 Speaker Overall, I'm pleased with this speaker. It hits the mark where it counts the most -- great sound. It makes the audio output of the Kindle Fire sound SO much better!

I also like that it runs on removable batteries. Many of the other small speakers I looked at had an internal rechargeable battery. While that has some advantages, the fact that the Fire does not have a USB port means I'd have to charge them from an outlet (with an adapter) or on my PC. Plus, non-removable batteries can present a problem when they fail. The Altec Lansing uses 3 AAA batteries which are far easier to deal with. I still use rechargeables (either Eneloops or the Amazon Basic rechargeable) and get several hours of play time per charge.

The shortcomings relate to the cord. It's short (about 8 inches) and is very thin. It would be a much better product with a longer cord (about 12 inches) and a cord that's made of more substantial material. I can see the cord being a potential point of failure down the road due to its lightweight construction.

But overall, it's a good device and a great value (if you catch it on a price dip). Highly recommend as an add-on to the Fire.
text_fidelity_b: Altec Lansing iM227 Orbit MP3 Speaker

I paired this with the [[ASIN:B000O161X0 Nikon 55-200mm f/4-5.6G ED IF AF-S DX VR [Vibration Reduction] Nikkor Zoom Lens]] for travel which is an even better deal.

text_fidelity_a:
SAMSUNG 75-Inch Class QLED 4K The Frame LS03B Series, Quantum HDR, Art Mode, Anti-Reflection Matte Display, Slim Fit Wall Mount Included, Smart TV w/ Alexa Built-In (QN75LS03BAFXZA, Latest Model) I am using this TV as my primary PC monitor. Since I don't have my PC stationed at a desk but rather use a wireless keyboard and mouse to remotely sit where I want to, the screen can be on my wall and I can comfortably sit back in my La-Z-Boy recliner several feet away while doing work, surfing the web, gaming, or whatever. This screen is really perfect for this, with a 120 hertz rate and 4k graphics. And of course it still maintains all the regular functionality of a TV as well.

I primarily use my computer to illustrate books for my day job, and this screen really makes my illustrations look great! Set to "Graphics" mode (rather than "Entertain" mode) the colors are true and the shadows retain great detail; the highlights are smooth, and clean. The color profile is easy to adjust. I really appreciate all of this very much. In the "Entertain" mode, the colors are amped up and the graphics are sharpened, etc. This is nice for watching films and gaming, but for doing graphics work it's absolutely necessary to have the colors and details represented accurately. The excellent anti-reflection and anti-glare features are also extremely helpful in this regard.

The native speakers are about what you would expect; they aren't amazing, but they aren't really all that bad for what this TV is intended to be either. It's really all about the screen. I personally don't care too much about the speakers, because 95% of the time that I use the screen I'm wearing headphones anyway so that I don't disturb my family. But if you're a real audiophile and that sort of thing is important to you, I would suggest you get some nice speakers to go with the TV, because the built-in speakers are clearly only meant to be just good enough to pass muster, and aren't anything to be wowed by.

For me, it's really nice that it doubles as a picture frame when I'm not actively using it for anything else. I have loaded an assortment of my own favorite photographs and illustrations for it to cycle through, and they look really great on this screen, but you can also access a fairly good assortment of art through the TV itself. This turns what is typically a bit of an eyesore in my opinion (I don't like the intrusive look of too much electronic technology in my home) into a lovely, active decoration instead.

I have not ordered a decorative frame to customize it; the reviews on those seem to indicate that they are perhaps overpriced and fragile, and I think it would be easy enough to make my own anyway, which I plan to do. I think having a frame on it would just be the cherry on top, so to speak.

And to reassure anyone who is wondering about the review that said this is the 2021 model, I think there must have been some confusion on one end or the other, because I definitely received the 2022 model that I ordered.

It came with the "Slim-Fit Wall Mount" included in the box (it's in the Styrofoam packing; I think another reviewer might have just not seen it, as it's not very large and it weighs much less than you might expect) along with a decent length of "One Invisible Connection" cable to attach it to the "One Connect Box" controller. This cable is just silver braid with a clear coating on it to help it blend in better than a regular black plastic cable. It serves as a power source as well as controlling the TV, so there's no bundle of unsightly cables hanging down from the screen.

The connect box replaces the usual bulk of the TV, which is what allows the screen to hang so flat on the wall like a regular picture frame. To use the TV, you'll need to position the One Connect box where you can use the remote to control it. It can be positioned anywhere so long as it's within reach of the cable. You can buy longer "One Invisible Connection" cables if necessary. The one that was included was long enough for my needs.
text_fidelity_b: SAMSUNG 75-Inch Class QLED 4K The Frame LS03B Series, Quantum HDR, Art Mode, Anti-Reflection Matte Display, Slim Fit Wall Mount Included, Smart TV w/ Alexa Built-In (QN75LS03BAFXZA, Latest Model)

Only reason I stopped using was the connectivity change. The new computers didn't offer the old PS2 connection.
So I was using other mice with USB connection before I bought this.
It was good in the beginning. After while, I started experiencing pointer freeze ALL THE TIME. It seems to reconnect periodically only when I don't need it. Then it disconnects when I need it the most. I'm still going back and forth to wired mice because of this.
At least I found a temporary solution, to flip the unit and turning off and on the switch. It works but is it something that Logitech expect all user to do? I don't know there maybe a way to fix this that I don't know yet. If somebody has a suggestion, I'll listen.

This was a HUGE disappointment.

*update* (9-28-16)
I decided to stop using it. Not worth the hustle. I started using since 8-31-16, the battery provided by Logitech is still new, 27 days old to be precise. I even tried another battery but the result was the same.
It's a piece of junk, I downgraded it to one star.

*update*(11-8-19)
I took it out and tried it again after years of not using it(original battery still in it).
It works now without freezing for prolonged time of use.
I have no idea what has changed, possibly automatic software update?
Anyway, I started using it regularly, again.

*update*(1-5-20)
Pointer freezing still persist occasionally.
I have found a temporary solution to it, turn the switch off and on again manually, then the pointer starts moving again.
It seems like it has something to do with "auto-sleep".
Does anybody know how to turn "auto-sleep" off?

My MacBook Pro’s display developed funky lines out of the blue, so it had to go in for a hardware repair. I write and save everything on my hard drive, so naturally I wanted a ton of backups. Just in case the worst happened and I ended up losing everything during the repair.

My appointment was set up for the next day, so I had little time to make a ton of backups. AND there was a massive thunderstorm, so the power kept flickering. I tried a normal stick first, and the estimated time was like 3 HOURS to copy everything. I so didn’t have time for that. I plugged the Sabrent in, started the copy, and went to get a drink. When I came back in less than five minutes, it was finished!!

I just now copied a 16gb folder in 48.15 seconds.

The USB-C adapter on the cord is also very handy, if you use the Sabrent on several computers or other devices. When I use the Sabrent on my MacBook Pro, I’m unable to plug anything else into the neighboring USB port because the adapter is blocky. But I’ll take the convenience of having one on the cord rather than having to go hunt for an adapter in my office.

The SSD itself is quite small. Very portable. The box the SSD comes in is great for storing the drive between uses, too. There’s a slightly padded interior compartment and a spot for the cord.

text_fidelity_a:
Blink Whole Home Bundle | Video Doorbell System, Outdoor camera, and Mini camera | HD video, motion detection, Works with Alexa "Set up in minutes"?? Not really. There are no actual detailed instructions included. I tried scanning the QR code that was provided in the little pamphlet, and that was not helpful. This ended up being extremely frustrating to set up. I could take a wild guess that I was supposed put the lithium batteries in the back of the camera. I would not have known that the little QR code inside the camera where the batteries go was something that I had to scan to set up the camera. Anyway, without going into detail, if Amazon provided some simple, basic instructions with photos that show step by step, it would save the customer a ton of fumbling around. Then it might have been an easy set up. I had to call for support, and by the time I got a support person on the phone I was pretty irritated. The reason I decided to buy this camera is the "two-year battery life." Note: these are not rechargeable batteries. We'll see how long the batteries last. Prior to this, I got a Eufy Solocam, also wireless (and much, much easier to set up), and it had rechargeable batteries advertised to last 4 months, but they lasted 4 weeks. A feature that is missing with the Blink camera, that I liked on the Eufy camera, is the AI feature to recognize humans. Without the AI feature, the Blink is recording non-human motion, such as animals and vehicles.

Update: The description advertises customized zones for motion detection. The camera takes a photo what it sees, and in motion settings, you gray out areas that you do not want the camera to detect motion. It does NOT work. I tried resetting it several times, and the camera recorded and sent me an alert of motion detected that was squarely in the grayed out area. Without this feature actually working, and without the AI feature to detect humans, the camera is recording every motion in the entire viewable area, ignoring the areas that I grayed out. I am returning this camera.
text_fidelity_b: Blink Whole Home Bundle | Video Doorbell System, Outdoor camera, and Mini camera | HD video, motion detection, Works with Alexa

It came formatted FAT (I think for Mac support), which means no support for files larger than 4 gig. I changed mine to NTFS to use in Linux and Windows. In Windows, the easy way to do that is with the convert command "convert <drive letter> /fs:ntfs" In Linux, it depends on your distro, but then, if you're only using Linux, you won't be using NTFS.

I built an Ubuntu Virtual Machine on the drive, and have been running it across multiple machines, as swiftly and easily as if the VM were stored locally. I can't think of a rougher stress test on performance, and it meets the challenge easily. It's rugged, reliable, and comes with built in drive encryption for your protection. Every OS I plug it into --Win 7, Win 8, Red Hat, Ubuntu, Debian -- recognizes it and mounts it with easy. It's so convenient. It holds my entire toolset. I never go anywhere without it.

text_fidelity_a:
Yamaha Audio SR-C20A Compact Sound Bar with Built-in Subwoofer and Bluetooth This SR-C20A is an entry-level Yamaha soundbar made for the smaller room and bedroom. The attraction to this model was the 3rd speaker, a powered subwoofer.

Most compact soundbars create bass through passive radiators integral with the bar … i.e. 2 powered speakers separated in width by a baffled tube radiating through holes. So, there is no controllable bass other than passive baffle sound effects.

The SR-C20A has a controllable powered subwoofer and a dual baffle radiator combined to deliver controllable high, medium, and low tones. There are five modes: standard, stereo, game, movie, and a virtual surround mode. I just picked the one that sounds best. The virtual surround provides a sense of depth and separation to my hearing.

The SR-C20A soundbar replaced a no-name 2-speaker with baffles. The difference is sizable sound improvement.

Easy install, lots of input options.

Better sound than expected. Impressive sound. Sized for the smaller room LCD/OLEAD TV. Priced right.
text_fidelity_b: Yamaha Audio SR-C20A Compact Sound Bar with Built-in Subwoofer and Bluetooth

This has been extremely frustrating and the time period, lack of communication within the company, and conflicting instructions told to me by employees are all unacceptable. I loved the TV but it failed and trying to get resolution from this company has been a nightmare.

UPDATE 1/25/16 7PM: About an hour after updating my review I was contacted by TCL. After two phone conversations and several emails a replacement is being processed with no shipping costs at my expense. If this occurs in the timely fashion expected, I will update my review and ratings accordingly.

UPDATE 1/25/16: A week after I got the TV it started having display problems. The screen would come on so dark that only by looking at it at a certain angle could you tell that it was on. It required a jiggle/tap on the top for the image to flicker on all the way. I contacted amazon tech support. They had me try a power off/unplug. I expressed concern that it appeared to be something internal failing. They said the recorded my comments and were willing to offer a refund. I really wanted a replacement and not a refund so I said I'd see if it stopped acting up. It did not. It got progressively worse and now never turns on correctly and no longer results to tapping and jiggling the TV. On

12/28 I emailed TCLsocial regarding my problem as it was getting worse. On 12/29 they responded asking for a phone number so they could call me. I immediately responded with my phone number. I received no calls. I was then extremely busy workign 16-18hr days 7 days a week. The next chance I got, I emailed them again 1/21. They responded that they hadn't received my phone number. I sent it again. They said I would "get a call within the day". As of 1/25 no calls, no missed calls, no voicemails no emails. I'm fed up. All I wanted was for them to replace my manufacturing defective item with a new one. Its terrible how poor their response at getting this dealt with has been. At least I know Amazon will make the refund quick and easy. But I will most certainly not be using the money to get another TCL brand if this is how they treat their customers. Picture below is my screen on "on". If you squint you can see a faint outline of the netflix box to the right of the flash reflection. This is not a brightness or display setting issue.

ORIGINAL REVIEW: Excellent TV, very simple and fast set up. Beautiful picture and great sound. Love the smart tv features. I do not have a roku device or account but I love this TV's features. The remote is a nice small size and very simple and intuitive. I highly recommend this model and am very satisfied thus far. text_fidelity_a:
Aokeo USB Microphone, Condenser Podcast Microphone for Computer. Suitable for Recording, Gaming, Desktop, Windows, Mac, YouTube, Streaming, Discord For the price this is a very nice USB microphone, I would agree with other reviewers that it performs on par with or better than similar competing USB condenser mics in this price range such as Blue Snowball or the Behringer C1.

I do wish it came with more accessories though similar to the non-USB version. The Aokeo AK-60 XLR version comes with a scissor boom arm, shock mount and pop filter for the same price.. so if you do happen to have a compatible audio interface with phantom power then I would recommend the XLR version.

The main annoyance with this mic is that when using it in windows 10 the driver does not have native mic gain control option. In many recording programs you can boost the mic gain via other means but if using this mic for gaming or other purposes through the native drivers then you will have to be very close to the mic to produce adequate volume (ie you pretty much need a boom arm) or otherwise you will need to boost gain via external passthrough program such as APO equalizer. I have also tried this mic in linux and the drivers there do have native gain control.

Overall I do think the sound quality and construction of the mic is good for the price and I would recommend it .. just note that if using windows 10 you will probably either need a boom arm or need to use external software to boost the mic gain. A boom arm is strongly recommended anyways to prevent extraneous noises like keyboard clacking, etc..
text_fidelity_b: Aokeo USB Microphone, Condenser Podcast Microphone for Computer. Suitable for Recording, Gaming, Desktop, Windows, Mac, YouTube, Streaming, Discord

Telescopes for Adults Astronomy, 70mm Aperture 400mm AZ Mount Astronomical Telescope for Astronomy Beginners Kids Adults - Carry Bag Upgraded Tripod and Phone Holder for Photography The telescope's purpose is to bird watch/identify visitors to the old-growth forest/marsh preserve adjoining our lot. I plan to keep the telescope 'permanent' through the second-story game room windows. We have a spectacular shot through the preserve. We live on a major migratory flyway. North American bird migrations and including the swarm of Monarch butterflies pass by the windows.

As to astronomical use, the refractor magnification lens system is entry-level. This general refractor-grade telescope serves as the smaller spotting scope on larger reflector telescopes. The scope has standard interfaces to mount better glass and wider angle lenses. It's a great basic platform to expand with higher quality and wider FOV lenses. I have plans to mount a made for purpose high res electronic magnification CCD to capture images. I've already replaced the tripod with a more robust design.

I'm delighted with the telescope as a basic platform for customizing. The main attraction is standard lens interfaces and scalability. The optical enhancements get pricey and will quickly exceed the purchase price.

Easy to assemble, easy to use. A beginner will get the hang of viewing with a little use with progressively smaller apertures as magnification is increased. There are viewing techniques available on YouTubes to investigate.

As expected and fully comparable to other refractor telescopes with a 70mm objective lens and 400mm focal length. Nice value for money.

text_fidelity_a:
Panasonic SC-HTB15 Home Theater System (2011 Model) You know how, with some movies, you can't hear the dialog for all the sound effects? This normalizes (or levels) the sound, so you can. It provides a better-than theater quality sound experience, for those of us who like to hear the dialog, experience the rich tones of the score, and not go deaf. Oh, it can get mighty loud if you want too. User's choice. It delivers a grand sound experience at any setting.

The setup is the "impress your kids" kind. It's easy, but it looks hard. You will need a Phillips head screwdriver, an [[ASIN:B003L1ZYYM AmazonBasics High-Speed HDMI Cable (6.5 Feet/2.0 Meters) - Supports Ethernet, 3D, and Audio Return [Newest Standard]]] and possibly (unless you have HDMI ARC) an [[ASIN:B001TH7GSW AmazonBasics Digital Optical Audio Toslink Cable, 6 Feet]]. Get them on Amazon. Most places charge a lot more for these. My TV didn't specifically state it was HDMI ARC (Audio Return Channel) but it worked anyway. I'm connected via an HDMI switcher, no problem. I just have the switch put out to the sound system, then the sound system put out to the TV. Everything is labelled and color coded, and it just couldn't be any easier. The only "gotcha" is make certain you're on the right input setting. Sometimes it wants TV instead of one of the HDMI ports.

It comes with a remote, in case your remote boat isn't already overflowing.

This is pretty much the top of the line. It's beautiful. It delivers awesome sound. It's perfect. I'm using my TV instead of my stereo to listen to music, because the sound quality of these speakers is that good. Oh, and you can turn the TV off and the speakers on, and the sound will still work.

text_fidelity_a:
Linksys WiFi Extender, WiFi 6 Range Booster, Dual-Band Booster, Internet Repeater, 2,000 Sq. ft Coverage, Speeds up to (AX1800) 1.8Gbps - RE7310 My experience with this extender has been good; it's significantly strengthened the signal in our living room, at the other end of the (admittedly not very big) house from our router. The one thing I've noticed is that nearby electrical devices, and especially ones with motors in them, will definitely throw this extender for a loop. We have an air purifier that lived first next to this extender, and then at a point about five feet from the extender, but between the extender and the router, and the extender did not like either of those situations at all. Lots of orange-light action (an orange light on this extender means no wifi signal). Moved the air purifier well away from the extender and out of the signal path and all was hunky-dory again.

I'm geeky sometimes and would like to be able to log onto the extender and muck with settings or at least make sure everything's good beyond what the green light tells me, but I don't seem to be able to do that once the extender's been set up; I can only get to the setup/configuration page after resetting the extender using the button on the back. But I'll live. The extender seems to be doing what we expect of it, and that's...all we expect of it (funny how that works).
text_fidelity_b: Linksys WiFi Extender, WiFi 6 Range Booster, Dual-Band Booster, Internet Repeater, 2,000 Sq. ft Coverage, Speeds up to (AX1800) 1.8Gbps - RE7310

text_fidelity_a:
Scosche MAGDM2 MagicMount Magnetic Car Phone Holder Mount - 360 Degree Adjustable Head, Universal with All Devices - Dashboard Mount This mount has been extremely useful in my vehicle. My CD player is right on the dash in a convenient spot to mount a device. This mount comes with the smaller metal plates made for cell phones and smaller devices. The large plate that is included with this mount works great on the back of my Samsung galaxy Tab. The 3M adhesive on these plates works fantastically. I have tried re-using these plates but I found that getting the plate off tends to bend it--even slightly. Once you bend these plates it does not re-use well. Included in the mount set, is a thin piece of plastic film that you can apply to your device in between the device and the plate. This makes it a lot easier to remove the plate from the device. This does a good job at making the re-use better.

The smaller plate works great on the back of my phones. I also use the plates inside of a phone case and they work great. The magnetic mount holds strong to phones and even tablets. I stuck the plate to the center of my tablet and I can stick the tablet onto the mount and utilize it without it falling off.

Dimensions of the plates and the mount can be seen in the photos I have uploaded.

Included:
-Large plate (with adhesive)
-Small plate (with adhesive)
-Plastic film plate/device separator
-Magnetic mount
-CD mount attachment

Pros:
*Holds a lot of weight (tablets)
*Easy to set up
*High quality adhesive
*Plenty of metal plates included

Cons:
*None

Additional Considerations:
You can get additional metal plates online. I also recommend all of scosche's mounts. Stuff is pretty interchangeable
.
Overall: 5/5 stars (>=.5 rounds up, <.5 rounds down) => 5 stars

If you have any further questions regarding the product in my review please leave a comment below and I will get back to you as soon as possible.

We simply love it.
Pros
Size. Very compact, takes up little space in wherever you store it and has a minimal footprint in use

Ease of use: set up was a few minutes and a breeze. As for actual usage, press a button and wait a bit. It will sometimes take a while to connect, but so far the longest has been ten minutes and that was once.
Usually it’s 3-5 minutes (and we have been in a lot of pretty remote places or tiny towns). Then connect to your device via your settings and you’re done. After that, it’s lwsys just auto connected with our two iPhones and one iPad with no issues connecting and no issues with dropping connection

speed: is it our home broadband? No. But it’s typically as good as our good hotels (and by “good” I mean Best Western/Quality Inn types— we’re not luxury travelers) and better than the cheap motels by a lot. That said, we stay almost exclusively in campgrounds and we haven’t deigned to use a campground wifi yet as they can’t compete to the Glocal for speed. They aren’t even in the ballpark. (We do try the camp wifi jut to compare).

The battery is great. We’ve charged it once in three weeks and it gets a lot of use. We’ve never been below a quarter charge

Can’t be happier
text_fidelity_b: GlocalMe DuoTurbo 4G LTE Portable WiFi Mobile Hotspot for Travel, with US 8GB & Global 1GB Data, No SIM Card Needed, Unlock Router Device for Home in 140+ Countries,Smart Local Network Auto-Selection
