text_fidelity_a:
Xiaomi YDXJ01FM Mi 4K Action Camera, 2.4” Touchscreen WiFi Sports Camera with Sony Image Sensor, 145° Wide Angle 4K/30fps 1080P/100fps Video Raw Image, Black I really wanted to like this camera. Construction quality is better than most budget-priced 4K action cameras. Price is much lower than GoPro. Battery life is great. Video quality is good for this price (but noticeably worse than GoPro and it lacks the 4K 60fps mode that GoPro has). Unfortunately, audio quality is poor.

A smartphone app is required to use much of the camera's functionality, including setting up the camera and all the wireless control features. I was able to download the app (a huge 75MB download to my Android phone). The app will not work until you create an account on Xiaomi's server in China. I am reluctant to send any of my personal information to an overseas corporation, but even when I tried to do it, I was unable to create the account, even after an hour of trying. The app does not work at all if I cannot login to the account.

A few more negatives about this camera. While the video quality is very good for this price level, audio recording quality is mediocre. This camera comes with no accessories in the box, just the camera, battery, brief instruction manual (more of the manual is in the app that I cannot use), and a charging cable (micro-USB, not USB-C like most modern devices). The camera uses a standard 1/4 inch tripod mount, but there is no GoPro-style action mount that would be much more sturdy and reliable if you are attaching the camera to a bicycle or helmet. There is no case to protect the camera from dirt or weather or use it underwater. Amazon does not sell any accessories either, so I don't know how to use this camera in an action situation. One battery is included in the box, but battery life is less than 2 hours and I always carry spares with my other action cameras. Again, Amazon does not sell spares.

Because of all these limitations, I can only give this camera 2 stars right now. Maybe if the app mysteriously starts working at some point and Amazon starts selling accessories to make the camera more usable, then I will consider reviewing the camera again.
text_fidelity_b: Xiaomi YDXJ01FM Mi 4K Action Camera, 2.4” Touchscreen WiFi Sports Camera with Sony Image Sensor, 145° Wide Angle 4K/30fps 1080P/100fps Video Raw Image, Black

Senso Bluetooth Headphones, Best Wireless Sports Earphones w/Mic IPX7 Waterproof HD Stereo Sweatproof Earbuds for Gym Running Workout 8 Hour Battery Noise Cancelling Headsets (Black Red) I have had way too many sets of headphones. Mostly because my dog eats them if they are within reach. While I still have not found the perfect headset with these, they come pretty close.

Durability and battery Life - Way too early to tell. I'll update this after a few months.

Noise Canceling- Let’s get something straight - if you put your fingers in your ears, they will cancel noise. That's called passive noise canceling, or simply, blocking outside noise. True active noise canceling head phones are over the ear, and usually very expensive. These head phones do a pretty good job passively blocking outside noise by fitting very well to the ear and being angled correctly.

Sound - Everyone has different tastes when it comes to what they like to hear. Some headphones have good or bad ranges from high to low. But it is the quality of the range that matters. For instance, I like to hear bass, and to me there is nothing worse than a tinny am radio sound. These definitely have bass, but it's a bit muddy. The good news is I was able to adjust the equalizer on my phone to clean it up, mostly. Overall all though, for the price, the sound quality is pretty darn good.

Fit & Hold - They Fit and stay put! The best part of these headphones is they fit my ears perfectly. The part that goes around the ear has a wire going through it, unlike so many others. This allows you to mold the over ear wires exactly to you ear and they do not fall out. None of the last several sets I had do this, and it is an enormous benefit.

Controls - The are typical up and down volume and a center button that is used for on, off, hold, answer, etc. I wish the volume buttons were reversed, but that's just being picky. They announce power on, power off and connected. Sadly, they do not announce battery life.

Appearance – Meh. They are a bit big and boxy, but I don’t know how that‘s different from having white things hanging out of your ears for $200.00

Overall - I am giving this 5 starts not because they are the best headphones. I am giving them 5 starts because they check off almost all of my boxes and the price it great. So, 5 stars for overall function and price.

Note: I paid full price for these and I was not asked to review them. Also, if you like this review, please indicate so below. Thanks.

text_fidelity_a:
woednx Smart Watch,1.4''Full Touch Fitness Tracker with Heart Rate,Blood Pressure and Sleep Monitor,Message Notification,Smartwatch for Men WomenIP68 Waterproof Smartwatch Sports for iOS Android-Blue PROS

1. The silicone band is very comfortable. Apparently if it breaks, it can be replaced, though I’m not sure where or how you would buy a new band.

2. The appearance is sleek and modern, and the size of the watch face makes the digital numbers easy to read.

3. It has a rechargeable battery, which may have a longer life than the non-rechargeable batteries of most sports watches.

4. If you want a smart watch that is far cheaper than most brands, this might work for you.

CONS

1. There are three primary functions that I use a sports watch for: to instantly check the time, a stopwatch, and a timer. It irritated me no end with this watch that, after only a few seconds of being lit up, its face goes dark. While this might save the charge on the rechargeable battery, there are plenty of times when my right hand it not free to punch the button on this watch to light up its face, and I can’t quickly and conveniently check the time! It is also a hassle trying to use the stopwatch and timer functions.

2. I absolutely loathe the way this watch’s battery is recharged. Instead of using a standard C cable, the charging cable attaches magnetically, and it becomes detached far too easily. There is also no warning when the battery of this watch is about to go dead.

3. I don’t like the software this phone uses. It is a major hassle to learn for what I personally consider very little useful return. Why? Because most of the functions offered by this watch that are of any interest to me I can get through my smartphone. I use my phone and a Bluetooth for phone calls, texting, music, and hearing alarms. I check the weather by looking around me when outside or looking at weather apps on my phone. I use my phone for photography.
The rest of the functions this watch offers I personally find to be useless. I do not need a watch to tell me how to do a deep breathing exercises. As a healthy individual with no heart issues, I do not need to monitor my heart rate 24/7. (And if I did, I would use medical equipment that is far more reliable than this cheap watch.) I don’t need to obsessively monitor my sleep. (And, again, if I did, I wouldn’t trust this cheap watch to do an accurate job of it.)

4. Its pedometer function might have been of use to me, but unfortunately, it is inaccurate.

CONCLUSION

text_fidelity_a:
iHome Smart Brief: 13 inch Laptop Briefcase for Mac, Heathered Grey Last year I switched to a Macbook Pro 13-inch after being a PC user since the early eighties. I love my Mac, but I haven't gone whole-hog for the rest of the pricey iProducts Apple puts out. Still, this case is just about perfect for my needs.

First, I like how the zippered compartment for the computer does not unzip all around. It's really easy to slip my Mac in and out of its fleecy padded pocket while still feeling like it's protected. (There's also plenty of room for my little wireless mouse dongle, although I don't use a mouse much anymore.) The iPad compartment is similar, and it holds my Kindle Fire in its rooCase with room to spare for something else (like a checkbook or wallet perhaps). The clever half-case compartment with pockets for chargers, headphones, and pens has plenty of room for my Mac power supply, Kindle charger and cables, and another charger if I need it.

The full compartment in the middle of the case is for whatever you might stick in it. It's not huge in depth, but it would certainly hold a legal pad/portfolio and a magazine or two. I don't use a cell phone now, but one day I might, so the outer pocket for the phone is nice; it's also serviceable for one of those small flashlights or perhaps a set of keys (on the right keychain). Toothbrush! I could see using the sleeve as a lapdesk/laptop stand while seated on a plane or in a doctor's office.

The sleeve comes with a classy, comfortable shoulder strap with strong, reliable clips. At first it wasn't clear what the the clips were supposed to clip to, but they are hidden away under the edges of the center gusset (what you see as the narrow black line running across the thickness in the photo here). There's no tangling up with this shoulder strap, either; the business ends can be rotated to keep the strap straight.

It's lightweight. And the color? It's a perfect match for the Mac Lion startup screen, of course. Everything about it says "Mac," including the iHome logo, but you don't have to be an Apple nut to love this sleeve. Very well designed.
text_fidelity_b: iHome Smart Brief: 13 inch Laptop Briefcase for Mac, Heathered Grey

If you just need a cable for charging your USB device, there are cheaper USB2.0 cables that will work just as well. Where these cables shine is data transfer. USB3.1 is tremendously faster than USB2.0 and these cables live up to the specification (as long as your devices support USB3.1). text_fidelity_a: Garmin nüvi 1390/1390T 4.3-Inch Bluetooth Portable GPS Navigator (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I have another Garmin unit (275T) and have had several Tom Tom systems. This unit is below the Garmin standards but significantly better then anything TomTom produces. The onboard memory is just barely sufficient to hold the NA maps. In fact, you have to remove languages in order to be able to load anything extra. While there is a slot for a micro sd card, it has very limited use. You can load an additional map OK. However if you load personal POI's onto it, every power on it pesters you to load them into the main memory - which, as mentioned, is very limited. Unlike my other 275T, there is no way to tell it to stop asking that question. Aside from the small memory problem and lack of reasonable support for the SD card, the unit works reasonably well. The enhanced lane guide is an interesting feature but I have found very few interchanges that are actually available for this capability. The standard lane guidance (just the arrows) work well enough. This has the typical Garmin problem that modifying the route is not possible, aside from telling it to avoid specific things (like highways, toll ways, u-turns, etc). I haven't used it a great deal yet but on the one major trip I took it did lose its end point once and decided to select some different destination. When I noticed that it kept trying to take me off the portion of the route I knew I should take, I selected the destination again and had it recalculate - then it was OK. So, as with all these units, it is a good idea to have a general idea of the route and not trust the unit completely. The Bluetooth feature seems to work OK but it is useless for me since I use a bluetooth earpiece instead.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin nüvi 1390/1390T 4.3-Inch Bluetooth Portable GPS Navigator (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin Portable Friction Mount - Frustration Free Packaging I've been using both, and the main difference in usability is that the beanbag mount has a lower initial stability and higher reserve stability than the fold-flat mount.
In other words, the fold-flat will stay put better - until it breaks free, when it becomes completely free with no holding power. The beanbag is a little easier to get to shift on a bounce, but then it has enough mass to settle stably in its new position.
On the whole I prefer the beanbag as I'd rather have my GPS move around a little bit more than have it stay put better but then fly around uncontrolled.
Other differences are that the fold-flat mount is lighter and folds up smaller, much better suited to stowing away or traveling.
The fold-flat also lets the GPS vibrate more, the beanbag dampens vibrations, but this can be overcome by pushing the GPS down in the fold-flat mount until it stays in contact with the base.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin Portable Friction Mount - Frustration Free Packaging

text_fidelity_a:
Arlo Pro - Wireless Home Security Camera System with Siren | Rechargeable, Night vision, Indoor/Outdoor, HD Video, 2-Way Audio, Wall Mount | Cloud Storage Included | 1 camera kit (VMS4130) After initial euphoria, I have to say that the ROI is marginal at best. Briefly, here is why:

Positive:
1. Excellent day and night picture quality
2. Simple configuration and UI.
3. Free storage up to limit.
4. Rugged construction
5. Integration with Smarthings and other IoT.
6. Easy setup. Ensure you buy the condoms and mounting brackets for outside.

Negative: (Relative to price point)
1. Battery life is marginal. If you never have motion in an area great. But, think about that front yard where you have people walking by or cars parked just on the edge of your property. With roughly 10-15 activation per day, the battery drains quickly. I feel I would be better off with a perm. powered device.
2. While it has a standard micro usb port similar to virtually any android smart phone. You still require the Arlo plug to charge. Not a deal breaker, but painful.
2. App load times/camera viewing is slow. I have a 100 mb Xfinity internet connection with Netgear Orbi Mesh setup within 15 ft of the front camera. Connection in my house is not the issue. I have a Samsung S7 device. Be prepared to wait upwards of 30 seconds before authentication, app loads AND THEN the camera activates to see who is at the front door. It needs to be faster.
3. The absolute worst aspect of the camera is that recording does not start fast enough. Roughly 30 seconds of an event (or more) go by before capture begins. This is not acceptable. I have tried playing with various settings but unable to resolve.

Overall, I regret purchasing now. I should have invested the time and installed a fixed camera setup.

12-Jul-17 - I have lowered the stars on this product because of the incredibly poor support provided for both this product and in particular the ORBI which I also have. The warranty on both products which are similarly priced make zero sense. Stay away from NETGEAR until they get their act together.

17-Aug-17 - Finally heard back from NETGEAR and received confirmation in their user forums that the original screw adapter on the VMA1000 mount for the solar panel is too big. (gee thanks..I knew that) I was sent new screws that now allow the solar cable to be plugged in along with the VMA1000 mount. Why these are not highlighted everywhere and why there is no update to the Amazon listing as a bulletin or something to look for when buying the solar panel, I don't know. Overall, I would say NETGEAR is completely lost on any form of cohesive support and sincerely hope my product continues to work as I do not want to ever have to call or email again..

June 2020
I am done with Arlo. The product is over-priced and unreliable. Here is why:
I added the doorbells 2 yes ago and 2 of 2 have been rma'd.
2 of the cameras have been rma'd.
1 of the 2 solar panels has apparently died as not properly charging. This after less than 2 years.
I only realized recently that some Einstein at Arlo decided to have the wifi channel operate on the exact channel my mesh is on. There are clearly issues.
The camera has good and bad days from an access perspective. Some days they come up in about 30 seconds. Some they don't load..
The delay of 5 seconds before motion activates recording is brutal. You can completely someone moving fast.
Arlo support has become poor after being fantastic initially.

This product will be going the way of my Orbi soon. I am done with Netgear ( or formerly Netgear) products...
text_fidelity_b: Arlo Pro - Wireless Home Security Camera System with Siren | Rechargeable, Night vision, Indoor/Outdoor, HD Video, 2-Way Audio, Wall Mount | Cloud Storage Included | 1 camera kit (VMS4130)
